observation.visible_scene: A beach at sunset. The sky fills the upper half with layered clouds: warm orange-yellow glow on the left, a small bright sun sitting just above the horizon slightly right of center, teal-blue cloud streaks across the top, and darker purple-grey cloud banks on the right. A band of breaking surf (white foam over dark water) runs horizontally across the middle. The foreground is a flat expanse of wet sand acting as a mirror, reflecting the orange and teal of the sky as large soft color patches. A thin sheet of water and a faint foam edge lie on the sand, with a curved 'tongue' of foam on the right and a small dark foam remnant near the center.
visible_changes: The surf line in the middle continuously breaks and reforms, its foamy lower edge wiggling and thickening/thinning frame to frame.

The thin water film and foam edge on the wet sand shift shape: the curved foam tongue on the right retreats slightly upward over the excerpt, while the faint diagonal water line on the left foreground moves downward, so the edge deforms rather than translating uniformly.
The small dark foam patch near the center of the beach fades and disappears by the later frames.
The orange and teal reflection patches on the foreground shimmer and subtly redistribute as the water film moves.
The sun, the horizon line, and the cloud arrangement stay essentially fixed throughout the segment (no detectable cloud drift or sun movement).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the overall tide/water level is rising or falling beyond this short window.
The full duration and any larger wave sets before or after this crop.
uncertain_details: The camera appears stationary (horizon and sun positions constant), but any very small drift cannot be fully excluded.
The exact direction and magnitude of the water-edge motion are small and partly ambiguous between frames.
The foreground color patches are reflections on wet sand, not separate objects, but their boundaries blend with the thin water sheet.
